events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Northern Coastal Humboldt
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking
waves 30 to 35 feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High
astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas
around Humboldt Bay. 1.5 to 2.2 feet of saltwater inundation
above ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal
waterways. Between 8.7 and 8.9 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide
gauge is predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, from 1 PM Friday to 4 AM PST
Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 11 AM to 3 PM PST
Friday. High tide is at 1:04pm at the Humboldt Bay North Spit
tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours
before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Breaking
waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into
dangerous seas. Life- threatening surf conditions and
significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...While astronomical tides are decreasing
each day, persistent southerly winds are aiding in raising water
levels for Humboldt Bay. The beginning of a very large incoming
swell could enhance coastal flooding if they overlap, but they
aren't anticipated to do so or will not overlap for long. After
only brief improvement in high swell late Saturday through
Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late Sunday through
Monday.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SMWLWX

The National Weather Service in Sterling Virginia has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Choptank River to Cambridge MD and the Little Choptank River...

* Until 715 PM EST.

* At 627 PM EST, a shower was located near Knapps Narrows Bridge,
moving east at 30 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Black Walnut Harbor weather station reported a 34 knot
gust.

IMPACT...Boaters in small craft could be thrown overboard by
suddenly higher winds and waves capsizing their vessel.

* Locations impacted include...
Choptank River.

Coastal waters from Manasquan Inlet to Little Egg Inlet NJ out 20
NM...

Waters from Manasquan Inlet NJ to Little Egg Inlet NJ from 20 to 60

At 627 PM EST, severe thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from 6 nm northeast of Sandy Hook Reef to 8 nm southwest of
Entrance to New York Harbor to near Shark River Reef to 10 nm east of
Axel Carlson Reef to near Barnegat Light Reef to Harvey Cedars,
moving southeast at 15 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves. Large hail could result in
structural damage.

Locations impacted include...
Sea Girt Reef, Barnegat Light, Shark River Reef, Seaside Park,
Barnegat Light Reef, Axel Carlson Reef, Sandy Hook Reef, Lavallette,
Harvey Cedars, and Forked River.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Monmouth, NJ; Ocean, NJ
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 626 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.5 to 1 inch in 1 hour.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned
area. Flash flooding is already occurring on NJ 35 north of Sylvania
Ave in Neptune City with lanes closed in both directions.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Long Branch, Asbury Park, Tinton Falls, Manasquan, Point Pleasant
Beach, Allenwood, Collingwood Park, Elberon, Ramtown, Point
Pleasant, Eatontown and West Long Branch.
